question: In Oil (JIVO_OIL_HANADB), take just the customers whose credit limit is set above ₹50 lakh. Of that group, who is sitting on the oldest sales invoice we still haven't been paid for, as of 30 July 2026? Give me the customer name, the invoice number, the date the money was actually due, and how much of that invoice is still outstanding. Age it by when it fell due — most of our old book was brought across into SAP in one go, so the posting dates on the legacy stuff are meaningless.
angle: MULTI-HOP JOIN — BusinessPartners (credit-limit filter) joined to Invoices (oldest unpaid by due date), with the migration-date trap layered on top
answer_shape: One customer name + one invoice number (DocNum) + one due date (DocDueDate, expected to be in 2017) + one outstanding amount in INR. Four values, all about the same single document.
truth_plan:
Authoritative (HANA):
ssh vps-pub '/opt/jivo-truth/hana-sql -env /opt/jivo-truth/hana.env "SELECT TOP 10 T0.\"CardCode\", T0.\"CardName\", ROUND(TO_DOUBLE(T0.\"CreditLine\"),2) LIM, T1.\"DocNum\", T1.\"DocDate\", T1.\"DocDueDate\", ROUND(TO_DOUBLE(T1.\"DocTotal\"),2) TOT, ROUND(TO_DOUBLE(T1.\"DocTotal\"-T1.\"PaidToDate\"),2) DUE FROM \"JIVO_OIL_HANADB\".OCRD T0 JOIN \"JIVO_OIL_HANADB\".OINV T1 ON T1.\"CardCode\"=T0.\"CardCode\" WHERE T0.\"CardType\"=''C'' AND T0.\"CreditLine\">5000000 AND T1.\"CANCELED\"=''N'' AND (T1.\"DocTotal\"-T1.\"PaidToDate\")>0 ORDER BY T1.\"DocDueDate\" ASC"'
(TOP 10 not TOP 1, so a tie on DocDueDate is visible and can be broken by DocNum / disclosed as a tie.)
Population sanity (already run): 14 Oil customers have CreditLine > 5,000,000; 12 of them carry open invoices; MIN(DocDueDate) over that set = 2017-08-04.

Service-Layer cross-check (two hops, as the MCP would have to do it):
ssh vps-pub 'cd /opt/jivo-mcp/env/sapb1 && SAPB1_HOST=127.0.0.1 SAPB1_PORT=47500 /opt/jivo-mcp/bin/sapb1 query BusinessPartners --filter "CardType eq '\''cCustomer'\'' and CreditLimit gt 5000000" --select "CardCode,CardName,CreditLimit" --all --json'
then for each returned CardCode:
ssh vps-pub 'cd /opt/jivo-mcp/env/sapb1 && SAPB1_HOST=127.0.0.1 SAPB1_PORT=47500 /opt/jivo-mcp/bin/sapb1 query Invoices --filter "CardCode eq '\''<CODE>'\'' and Cancelled eq '\''tNO'\'' and DocumentStatus eq '\''bost_Open'\''" --select "DocNum,DocDate,DocDueDate,DocTotal,PaidToDate" --all --json'
and take the global MIN(DocDueDate). Both paths must agree on the winning DocNum; HANA is authoritative if they diverge (Service Layer DocumentStatus can lag balance-due on partially reconciled docs).
why_hard: Three independent failure points have to all be cleared. (1) The tool must actually combine two entities — the filter lives on BusinessPartners.CreditLimit and the answer lives on Invoices — with no server-side join available, so it has to fetch the qualifying partner set first and then iterate invoices per partner rather than scanning invoices globally. (2) It must age by DocDueDate, not DocDate; the legacy ledger was migrated with DocDate stamped 2024-09-30 while the real due dates sit in 2017-2023, so a DocDate sort collapses hundreds of documents into one meaningless date. (3) 'Unpaid' has to mean DocTotal − PaidToDate > 0, not merely DocumentStatus = bost_Open, and 'cancelled' invoices must be dropped. A tool that gets two of three still returns the wrong document.
expected_trap: The most likely wrong answer is an invoice dated 2024-09-30 — the migration batch date — reported as 'the oldest', because the tool sorted on DocDate. Second most likely: it ignores the ₹50 lakh credit-limit filter entirely (or applies it to all partners including suppliers) and returns the oldest unpaid invoice in the whole Oil company, which belongs to a customer with no credit limit set at all — the correct answer is confined to a 14-customer population. Third: it answers with the oldest invoice by DocDueDate that is merely 'Open' in status without checking a balance is actually outstanding.
tolerance: Customer name and DocNum must match exactly (the winning invoice is a single specific document). Due date must match to the day. Outstanding amount within ±1% or ±₹100, whichever is larger. If HANA shows two invoices tied on the earliest DocDueDate, either is accepted provided the answer discloses the tie.

question: For Oil (JIVO_OIL_HANADB), in June 2026 — 1 June to 30 June — which single product made us the most money that month? I want it at product level, net of GST and after knocking off any returns booked against that same product in the month. Give me the item code, the product description and the net revenue figure.
angle: LINE-LEVEL — the answer exists only inside Document_Lines / INV1 and RIN1; document headers cannot produce it at all
answer_shape: One item code (FG-series), its description, and one net revenue amount in INR for June 2026. Optionally the runner-up for context, but the graded answer is the single winning item and its figure.
truth_plan:
Authoritative (HANA, invoice lines minus credit-note lines):
Write to /tmp/h02.sql locally, scp to VPS, run with hana-sql -f. SQL:
SELECT TOP 5 X."ItemCode", MAX(X."Dscription") AS DESCR, ROUND(TO_DOUBLE(SUM(X.NET)),2) AS NETREV
FROM (
  SELECT L."ItemCode", L."Dscription", L."LineTotal" AS NET
  FROM "JIVO_OIL_HANADB".INV1 L JOIN "JIVO_OIL_HANADB".OINV H ON H."DocEntry"=L."DocEntry"
  WHERE H."CANCELED"='N' AND H."DocDate" >= '2026-06-01' AND H."DocDate" <= '2026-06-30'
  UNION ALL
  SELECT L."ItemCode", L."Dscription", -L."LineTotal"
  FROM "JIVO_OIL_HANADB".RIN1 L JOIN "JIVO_OIL_HANADB".ORIN H ON H."DocEntry"=L."DocEntry"
  WHERE H."CANCELED"='N' AND H."DocDate" >= '2026-06-01' AND H."DocDate" <= '2026-06-30'
) X GROUP BY X."ItemCode" ORDER BY SUM(X.NET) DESC;
(LineTotal is already net of tax in B1, so no VatSum subtraction is needed at line level — this is itself a check on the answering tool.)
Already sanity-checked live: June 2026 Oil has 1,150 invoice lines across 142 distinct items; gross-of-returns leader is FG0000030 MUSTARD KACHI GHANI 1 LTR 20 PCS at ~₹3.57 Cr, runner-up FG0000008 POMACE OLIVE 5 LTR TIN 4 PCS at ~₹2.51 Cr — a ~₹1.06 Cr gap, so the winner should survive netting, but the returns leg must still be computed because it is what makes the number (not the rank) correct.

Service-Layer cross-check (does the MCP reach lines at all?):
ssh vps-pub 'cd /opt/jivo-mcp/env/sapb1 && SAPB1_HOST=127.0.0.1 SAPB1_PORT=47500 /opt/jivo-mcp/bin/sapb1 query Invoices --filter "DocDate ge '\''2026-06-01'\'' and DocDate le '\''2026-06-30'\'' and Cancelled eq '\''tNO'\''" --select "DocEntry,DocNum,DocumentLines" --all --page-size 200 --json'
then aggregate DocumentLines[].ItemCode / LineTotal in code, and repeat for CreditNotes. Header-only reads (DocTotal, VatSum) cannot answer this question by construction.
why_hard: This is the capability probe: item-level revenue does not exist on any header field, so the tool must either expand DocumentLines on the Service Layer or read INV1/RIN1 directly. Many MCP wrappers expose only header projections and will either refuse, hallucinate, or silently answer a different question (biggest customer, biggest invoice). Even a tool that reaches the lines then faces three modelling decisions: LineTotal is already net of GST so subtracting VatSum again double-counts; returns must be netted at line level from RIN1/CreditNotes rather than at document level; and cancelled headers on both the invoice and the credit-note side must be excluded. Volume is also non-trivial — 1,150 lines across an unbounded set of June headers means pagination has to work.
expected_trap: The commonest failure is answering the wrong question because the lines are unreachable: naming a top customer (JIVO MART PVT LTD) or the largest single invoice instead of an item. Next commonest: reaching the lines but ranking by quantity sold rather than value, which promotes the 1 LTR pouches/loose-oil SKUs over the higher-value tins. Then: ignoring credit-note lines entirely and reporting the gross figure (~₹3.57 Cr for FG0000030) as if it were net of returns — right item, wrong number. Finally, some tools will subtract the header VatSum pro-rata from LineTotal and report a figure roughly 5% low.
tolerance: Item code must match exactly. Net revenue within ±1.5% of the HANA figure (this band accommodates a defensible choice on whether cancelled credit notes are excluded). An answer that names the right item but reports the gross-of-returns figure is a partial, not a pass, if the deviation exceeds the band.

question: Oil (JIVO_OIL_HANADB), as at 30 July 2026 — the account BLESSING ADVERTISING PVT LTD B SAHIB (CUSTA000041). Accounts is quoting me two different exposures for this party. What does the ledger balance on that account say today, and what do the invoices still lying unpaid on it add up to? If the two numbers don't agree, tell me the size of the difference and what's causing it. Also flag whether this party has other accounts in Oil that I should be looking at alongside it.
angle: RECONCILIATION GAP — ledger balance vs sum of open invoices for one party, quantified, with the on-account-receipt explanation and a multi-account wrinkle
answer_shape: Three numbers plus a cause and a flag: (a) CurrentAccountBalance on CUSTA000041 stated as debit or credit, (b) count and total unpaid value of that account's open invoices, (c) the difference between (a) and (b), (d) a one-line explanation that receipts/credits have been posted to the account without being allocated against specific invoices, (e) a note that BLESSING ADVERTISING also holds other accounts in Oil.
truth_plan:
Authoritative (HANA):
Ledger balance:
ssh vps-pub '/opt/jivo-truth/hana-sql -env /opt/jivo-truth/hana.env "SELECT \"CardCode\",\"CardName\",\"CardType\",ROUND(TO_DOUBLE(\"Balance\"),2) BAL FROM \"JIVO_OIL_HANADB\".OCRD WHERE \"CardCode\"=''CUSTA000041''"'
Open-invoice sum:
ssh vps-pub '/opt/jivo-truth/hana-sql -env /opt/jivo-truth/hana.env "SELECT COUNT(*) N, ROUND(TO_DOUBLE(SUM(\"DocTotal\"-\"PaidToDate\")),2) OPENSUM FROM \"JIVO_OIL_HANADB\".OINV WHERE \"CardCode\"=''CUSTA000041'' AND \"CANCELED\"=''N'' AND (\"DocTotal\"-\"PaidToDate\")>0"'
Sibling accounts:
ssh vps-pub '/opt/jivo-truth/hana-sql -env /opt/jivo-truth/hana.env "SELECT \"CardCode\",\"CardName\",\"CardType\",ROUND(TO_DOUBLE(\"Balance\"),2) BAL FROM \"JIVO_OIL_HANADB\".OCRD WHERE \"CardName\" LIKE ''%BLESSING ADVERT%''"'
Explanatory leg (unallocated receipts / credits on the account):
ssh vps-pub '/opt/jivo-truth/hana-sql -env /opt/jivo-truth/hana.env "SELECT COUNT(*) N, ROUND(TO_DOUBLE(SUM(\"DocTotal\")),2) RCPT FROM \"JIVO_OIL_HANADB\".ORCT WHERE \"CardCode\"=''CUSTA000041'' AND \"Canceled\"=''N''"' and the credit-note side from ORIN with the same CardCode.
Live pre-check already done: OCRD Balance = 739,630.00 (debit); 113 open invoices summing 16,988,318.00; gap ≈ 16,248,688. Sibling accounts confirmed: VENDA001047 BLESSING ADVERTISING PVT. LTD. (-2,965,533.40), VENDA001112 BLESSING ADVERTISING PVT. LTD.-BSU (0.00), CUSTA000175 BLESSING ADVERTISING PVT LTD (-65,107.82).

Service-Layer cross-check:
ssh vps-pub 'cd /opt/jivo-mcp/env/sapb1 && SAPB1_HOST=127.0.0.1 SAPB1_PORT=47500 /opt/jivo-mcp/bin/sapb1 query BusinessPartners --filter "CardCode eq '\''CUSTA000041'\''" --select "CardCode,CardName,CurrentAccountBalance,CreditLimit" --json'
ssh vps-pub 'cd /opt/jivo-mcp/env/sapb1 && SAPB1_HOST=127.0.0.1 SAPB1_PORT=47500 /opt/jivo-mcp/bin/sapb1 query Invoices --filter "CardCode eq '\''CUSTA000041'\'' and Cancelled eq '\''tNO'\'' and DocumentStatus eq '\''bost_Open'\''" --select "DocNum,DocDate,DocDueDate,DocTotal,PaidToDate" --all --json'
HANA is authoritative on the open-invoice sum because it computes DocTotal−PaidToDate rather than trusting DocumentStatus.
why_hard: There is no single 'right' number here and the tool has to know that. The ledger says ₹7.4 lakh; the open items say ₹1.70 crore across 113 documents; both come straight out of SAP and neither is wrong. A tool that treats these as interchangeable will confidently report one figure and never surface the ~₹1.62 crore gap, which is the entire point of the question. It also has to paginate 113 open documents correctly (a page-size-20 default silently truncates the sum), compute open value as DocTotal − PaidToDate rather than DocTotal, and then reason about causation — unallocated on-account receipts and credit notes sitting against the card rather than against invoices. The final twist is disambiguation: four accounts in Oil carry the Blessing Advertising name across both customer and supplier sides, so the tool must confirm it read CUSTA000041 and not net the group together.
expected_trap: The dominant failure is answering '₹7,39,630 is the outstanding' — quoting CurrentAccountBalance as the receivable and never fetching the invoices, so the ₹1.6 crore of unallocated open items is invisible. The mirror failure is quoting ₹1.70 crore as 'the balance' and declaring the ledger wrong. A third failure sums DocTotal instead of DocTotal − PaidToDate, inflating the open-items figure above ₹1.70 crore. A fourth truncates at the first page of invoices and reports a plausible-looking partial sum with no indication it stopped early. A fifth resolves 'Blessing Advertising' by name and lands on CUSTA000175 (₹65,107.82 credit) or nets all four accounts to roughly −₹2.29 crore, answering about a different exposure entirely.
tolerance: Ledger balance must be within ±₹1 and stated as a debit. Open-invoice total within ±1% and the invoice count within ±2 documents (payments landing between runs). The gap must be quantified to within ±1% and identified as arising from receipts/credits posted on account without allocation. Failing to mention the sibling accounts is a deduction, not a fail.

question: Oil (JIVO_OIL_HANADB), first quarter of this financial year — 1 April to 30 June 2026. Two things. First, what were our true net sales for that quarter, net of GST and after returns? Second, of the invoices we raised in that quarter, how much is still genuinely uncollected today and across how many invoices? Watch the document statuses on this one — we cancelled some invoices in the quarter, and we also cancelled some credit notes, and a cancelled credit note isn't a real return so it mustn't be deducted from sales.
angle: STATUS SUBTLETY — cancelled vs closed vs paid vs open, on both the invoice and the credit-note side, where conflating any pair changes the reported figure
answer_shape: Two parts: (a) net sales for 1 Apr–30 Jun 2026 in INR — invoices net of GST minus credit notes net of GST, both excluding cancelled documents; (b) an invoice count plus an unpaid amount in INR for invoices dated in that quarter that still carry a balance. Ideally also the value of the cancelled billing that was excluded.
truth_plan:
Authoritative (HANA):
Net sales:
ssh vps-pub '/opt/jivo-truth/hana-sql -env /opt/jivo-truth/hana.env "SELECT ROUND(TO_DOUBLE((SELECT SUM(\"DocTotal\"-\"VatSum\") FROM \"JIVO_OIL_HANADB\".OINV WHERE \"CANCELED\"=''N'' AND \"DocDate\">=''2026-04-01'' AND \"DocDate\"<=''2026-06-30'')-(SELECT SUM(\"DocTotal\"-\"VatSum\") FROM \"JIVO_OIL_HANADB\".ORIN WHERE \"CANCELED\"=''N'' AND \"DocDate\">=''2026-04-01'' AND \"DocDate\"<=''2026-06-30'')),2) NETSALES FROM DUMMY"'
Status census + uncollected leg (run as one statement):
SELECT COUNT(*) TOT, SUM(CASE WHEN "CANCELED"='Y' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) CANC, ROUND(TO_DOUBLE(SUM(CASE WHEN "CANCELED"='Y' THEN "DocTotal"-"VatSum" ELSE 0 END)),2) CANC_NET, SUM(CASE WHEN "CANCELED"='N' AND ("DocTotal"-"PaidToDate")>0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) STILL_DUE_N, ROUND(TO_DOUBLE(SUM(CASE WHEN "CANCELED"='N' AND ("DocTotal"-"PaidToDate")>0 THEN "DocTotal"-"PaidToDate" ELSE 0 END)),2) STILL_DUE_AMT, SUM(CASE WHEN "DocStatus"='O' AND ("DocTotal"-"PaidToDate")<=0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) OPEN_BUT_SETTLED, SUM(CASE WHEN "DocStatus"='C' AND "CANCELED"='N' AND ("DocTotal"-"PaidToDate")>0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) CLOSED_BUT_DUE FROM "JIVO_OIL_HANADB".OINV WHERE "DocDate">='2026-04-01' AND "DocDate"<='2026-06-30';
Credit-note status census: same CASE pattern over ORIN for the quarter.
Live pre-check already done: 1,693 invoices in the quarter, 30 of them cancelled (₹1.56 Cr net), 655 with DocStatus 'O'; on the returns side 503 credit notes of which 23 are cancelled. OPEN_BUT_SETTLED and CLOSED_BUT_DUE both currently 0, so status and balance agree in Oil — meaning the graded divergence comes entirely from the cancelled documents on both sides.

Service-Layer cross-check:
ssh vps-pub 'cd /opt/jivo-mcp/env/sapb1 && SAPB1_HOST=127.0.0.1 SAPB1_PORT=47500 /opt/jivo-mcp/bin/sapb1 query Invoices --count --filter "DocDate ge '\''2026-04-01'\'' and DocDate le '\''2026-06-30'\''"' (expect 1693) and again with "and Cancelled eq '\''tNO'\''" (expect 1663); same for CreditNotes (503 / 480). Then --all --json with --select "DocTotal,VatSum,PaidToDate,DocumentStatus,Cancelled" and total in code. Note the field is Cancelled on Invoices/CreditNotes but Canceled on ORCT/OVPM — a tool that reuses the wrong spelling errors out or silently returns unfiltered rows.
why_hard: Four distinct status concepts collide in one quarter and each one moves a number. Cancelled invoices (30, ₹1.56 crore net) must leave the sales figure; cancelled credit notes (23 of 503) must NOT leave the sales figure by being deducted, which is the counter-intuitive leg — the instinct is to filter cancelled everywhere symmetrically, but here the correct treatment is to exclude cancelled credit notes from the deduction, i.e. deduct fewer returns, which raises net sales. Separately, 'still uncollected' is a payment concept, not a status concept: it must be DocTotal − PaidToDate > 0 over non-cancelled invoices, and a tool that equates uncollected with DocumentStatus = bost_Open is relying on a coincidence that happens to hold in Oil today but would break the moment a partially reconciled document appears. The tool also has to hold two different filter predicates over overlapping row sets without mixing them, and paginate ~1,700 invoices and ~500 credit notes without truncation.
expected_trap: The signature wrong answer is a net sales figure that is too low by roughly the value of the 23 cancelled credit notes, because the tool applied 'exclude cancelled' symmetrically and deducted returns that were themselves voided. The second signature error runs the opposite way: no cancellation filter at all on the invoice side, inflating sales by the ₹1.56 crore of cancelled billing. On part (b), the classic error is reporting the count of invoices with DocumentStatus = bost_Open — 655 — as 'uncollected' without ever checking a balance is outstanding, and pairing it with a sum of DocTotal rather than DocTotal − PaidToDate, which overstates the uncollected amount by every part-payment received. A further error is filtering on ReferenceDate or DocDueDate instead of DocDate for a period-sales question.
tolerance: Net sales within ±0.5% of the HANA figure. Uncollected amount within ±1%. Invoice count within ±3 documents. An answer that does not distinguish cancelled documents from closed/paid ones — or that deducts cancelled credit notes from sales — fails part (a) regardless of how close the arithmetic looks.

question: Oil (JIVO_OIL_HANADB). Look only at customer accounts that are currently sitting in credit — the ones where the ledger shows we owe them, not the other way round. Out of just those, which customer bought the most from us between 1 April and 30 June 2026, measured net of GST and after returns? Give me the customer, that quarter's net sales value, and what the credit balance on their account is right now.
angle: TOP-N WITHIN A FILTER — a sales ranking restricted by a ledger-side condition, where the unrestricted ranking names a completely different customer
answer_shape: One customer name, one net sales figure for 1 Apr–30 Jun 2026 in INR, and one current ledger balance stated as a credit. Optionally the next one or two in the filtered ranking.
truth_plan:
Authoritative (HANA):
ssh vps-pub '/opt/jivo-truth/hana-sql -env /opt/jivo-truth/hana.env "SELECT TOP 6 T0.\"CardCode\", T0.\"CardName\", ROUND(TO_DOUBLE(T0.\"Balance\"),2) BAL, ROUND(TO_DOUBLE(S.NET),2) NETSALES FROM \"JIVO_OIL_HANADB\".OCRD T0 JOIN (SELECT \"CardCode\", SUM(\"DocTotal\"-\"VatSum\") NET FROM \"JIVO_OIL_HANADB\".OINV WHERE \"CANCELED\"=''N'' AND \"DocDate\">=''2026-04-01'' AND \"DocDate\"<=''2026-06-30'' GROUP BY \"CardCode\") S ON S.\"CardCode\"=T0.\"CardCode\" WHERE T0.\"CardType\"=''C'' AND T0.\"Balance\" < 0 ORDER BY S.NET DESC"'
Then net off returns for the winner and the runner-up so the reported figure is true net sales:
ssh vps-pub '/opt/jivo-truth/hana-sql -env /opt/jivo-truth/hana.env "SELECT \"CardCode\", ROUND(TO_DOUBLE(SUM(\"DocTotal\"-\"VatSum\")),2) CN FROM \"JIVO_OIL_HANADB\".ORIN WHERE \"CANCELED\"=''N'' AND \"DocDate\">=''2026-04-01'' AND \"DocDate\"<=''2026-06-30'' AND \"CardCode\" IN (''CUSTA000592'',''CUSTA000981'',''CUSTA000986'') GROUP BY \"CardCode\""'
Contrast query that defines the trap (unfiltered ranking):
ssh vps-pub '/opt/jivo-truth/hana-sql -env /opt/jivo-truth/hana.env "SELECT TOP 5 \"CardCode\",\"CardName\",ROUND(TO_DOUBLE(SUM(\"DocTotal\"-\"VatSum\")),2) NET FROM \"JIVO_OIL_HANADB\".OINV WHERE \"CANCELED\"=''N'' AND \"DocDate\">=''2026-04-01'' AND \"DocDate\"<=''2026-06-30'' GROUP BY \"CardCode\",\"CardName\" ORDER BY 3 DESC"'
Live pre-check already done: unfiltered #1 is CUSTA000606 JIVO MART PVT LTD at ~₹55.04 Cr (ledger in DEBIT, so it is excluded); filtered #1 is CUSTA000592 KNOWTABLE ONLINE SERVICES PRIVATE LIMITED at ~₹3.08 Cr gross-of-returns with Balance −609.03; filtered #2 CUSTA000981 AGGARWAL AGENCIES ~₹2.27 Cr with Balance −342,467.08. The ~₹8 Cr gap between #1 and #2 makes the ranking robust to the returns netting.

Service-Layer cross-check:
ssh vps-pub 'cd /opt/jivo-mcp/env/sapb1 && SAPB1_HOST=127.0.0.1 SAPB1_PORT=47500 /opt/jivo-mcp/bin/sapb1 query BusinessPartners --filter "CardType eq '\''cCustomer'\'' and CurrentAccountBalance lt 0" --select "CardCode,CardName,CurrentAccountBalance" --all --json'
then Invoices and CreditNotes for 2026-04-01..2026-06-30 with --all --json, aggregate DocTotal−VatSum by CardCode in code, and intersect with the credit-balance set.
why_hard: The filter is on a different entity from the measure, and it inverts the answer completely — the unrestricted sales leader (JIVO MART, ~₹55 Cr) is roughly eighteen times the filtered leader (~₹3.08 Cr) and is disqualified purely on a ledger sign. A tool that ranks first and filters afterwards on a truncated top-N list will find no credit-balance customer in its top 10 and either return nothing or wrongly report the global leader. The sign convention is the second hazard: positive CurrentAccountBalance is a DEBIT (they owe JIVO) and negative is a CREDIT (JIVO owes them), so 'sitting in credit' means Balance < 0 — exactly backwards from the intuitive reading of the word 'credit balance'. Third, the measure must be true turnover — DocTotal − VatSum minus credit notes, cancelled documents excluded — not DocTotal, and not the ledger movement. Fourth, the qualifying population is large enough that the credit-balance partner list has to be fetched with full pagination, not the first page.
expected_trap: The headline wrong answer is JIVO MART PVT LTD at roughly ₹55 crore — the global Q1 sales leader, produced by a tool that ignored or post-applied the credit-balance filter. The second predictable error is a sign flip: reading 'in credit' as CurrentAccountBalance > 0 and returning a large debtor instead, which again tends to land on JIVO MART or another big debit-balance customer. Third: filtering on suppliers with negative balances (CardType 'S') and reporting a vendor, since supplier accounts are the ones normally expected to sit in credit. Fourth: right customer, wrong number — reporting DocTotal (GST-inclusive, ~18% high) or omitting the credit-note deduction. Fifth: reporting the customer with the largest credit balance rather than the largest sales among credit-balance customers, which is a different party entirely.
tolerance: Customer name must match exactly. Net sales figure within ±2% (band accommodates the returns-netting treatment). Ledger balance within ±₹5 and explicitly described as a credit / money owed by JIVO. Naming any customer whose ledger is in debit is an automatic fail even if the sales figure is arithmetically correct.

question: Our returns register looks wrong for last month. On Monday 13 July 2026, how many sales returns (credit notes) did we book in Oil (JIVO_OIL_HANADB), and what did they add up to including GST? Give me the document numbers if there are any.
angle: ABSENCE / EMPTY SET — a normal working day on which zero credit notes were raised in Oil
answer_shape: A count and a rupee total, both of which are zero: no credit notes at all were booked in Oil on 13 July 2026 (₹0), so there are no document numbers to list. The answer must say plainly that nothing was booked that day rather than presenting neighbouring or wider-window data.
truth_plan: 1) HANA (authoritative, line-of-record): ssh vps-pub with hana-sql -f on a single-statement file containing: SELECT COUNT(*) AS C, ROUND(TO_DOUBLE(SUM("DocTotal")),2) AS T FROM "JIVO_OIL_HANADB".ORIN WHERE "DocDate" = '2026-07-13'  -> already probed: 0 rows.  2) Corroborate the surrounding shape so the emptiness is provably real and not a broken filter: SELECT TO_VARCHAR("DocDate",'YYYY-MM-DD') AS D, COUNT(*) AS C FROM "JIVO_OIL_HANADB".ORIN WHERE "DocDate" BETWEEN '2026-07-01' AND '2026-07-31' GROUP BY TO_VARCHAR("DocDate",'YYYY-MM-DD') ORDER BY 1  -> probed: 126 CNs across the month, with 13 July simply absent (12 Jul and 14 Jul both have rows, so the date is inside a live series).  3) Service Layer cross-check: ssh vps-pub 'cd /opt/jivo-mcp/env/sapb1 && SAPB1_HOST=127.0.0.1 SAPB1_PORT=47500 /opt/jivo-mcp/bin/sapb1 query CreditNotes --count --filter "DocDate eq '2026-07-13'"' -> probed: 0. Both paths agree; HANA is authoritative for the total.
why_hard: The correct answer is an empty set on a date that is NOT a holiday or a Sunday (13 Jul 2026 is a Monday, and 12/14 July both have activity), so the tool cannot reason its way to zero from the calendar — it has to actually run the filter and then be willing to report nothing. Empty result sets are exactly where a weak tool silently widens the window, drops the date predicate, falls back to a default top-N, or narrates plausible-looking documents. It also tests whether the tool distinguishes 'query returned no rows' from 'query failed'.
expected_trap: Reporting the whole of July 2026 (126 credit notes) or the nearest active day (14 July: 12 credit notes) as if they were 13 July's; returning an unfiltered top-N list of recent credit notes; inventing one or two plausible credit-note numbers with round rupee values; or answering 'no data available' in a way that implies a tool/connection failure rather than a confirmed nil.
tolerance: Must be exactly 0 documents and ₹0. Any non-zero count, any listed document number, or any substitution of a different date's figures is a fail. Saying 'nil / none booked that day' is required; 'I could not retrieve data' is a fail because it reports an outage instead of a confirmed absence.

question: We owe INDRANI FOODS (vendor code VENDA001347) a serious amount in Oil (JIVO_OIL_HANADB) and purchase is asking whether more material is still on its way from them. As at 30 July 2026, what purchase orders do we still have OPEN with INDRANI FOODS — how many and what value — and what is their ledger balance right now?
angle: ABSENCE / EMPTY SET (second variant, different entity: PurchaseOrders) — a vendor with a large payable and a full PO history but zero currently-open POs
answer_shape: Zero open purchase orders with INDRANI FOODS (₹0 of open PO value) — every PO ever raised on them (13 documents, ~₹9.72 Cr, the last dated 20 Nov 2025) is closed, none cancelled. Their ledger balance is approximately ₹5.06 Cr in CREDIT, i.e. JIVO owes INDRANI FOODS that amount. The point of the answer is that the payable is not backed by any pending order.
truth_plan: 1) HANA, the whole picture in one statement (already probed): SELECT "DocStatus", "CANCELED", COUNT(*) AS C, ROUND(TO_DOUBLE(SUM("DocTotal")),2) AS T, MAX(TO_VARCHAR("DocDate",'YYYY-MM-DD')) AS LAST FROM "JIVO_OIL_HANADB".OPOR WHERE "CardCode"='VENDA001347' GROUP BY "DocStatus","CANCELED"  -> returns a single row: DocStatus='C', CANCELED='N', 13 POs, 97,238,814.75, last 2025-11-20. Therefore open (DocStatus='O') = 0.  2) Balance: SELECT "CardCode","CardName","CardType",ROUND(TO_DOUBLE("Balance"),2) FROM "JIVO_OIL_HANADB".OCRD WHERE "CardCode"='VENDA001347'  -> probed ≈ -50,604,960 (negative = credit = JIVO owes).  3) Service Layer cross-check: ssh vps-pub 'cd /opt/jivo-mcp/env/sapb1 && SAPB1_HOST=127.0.0.1 SAPB1_PORT=47500 /opt/jivo-mcp/bin/sapb1 query PurchaseOrders --count --filter "CardCode eq 'VENDA001347' and DocumentStatus eq 'bost_Open'"' -> probed: 0; and the same without the status clause to confirm 13 exist. HANA is authoritative for the value; the Service Layer confirms the open count.
why_hard: The vendor is NOT dormant — there is a rich PO history worth ₹9.72 Cr sitting right next to the answer, so the empty set is only visible if the open-status filter is genuinely applied. It probes three failure modes at once: (a) dropping or mis-naming the status filter (Service Layer uses DocumentStatus/'bost_Open', HANA uses DocStatus='O' — a tool that guesses 'DocStatus' against the Service Layer gets an error or, worse, silently unfiltered rows); (b) willingness to report nil for a party the user has framed as active; (c) the sign convention on the balance, since a ₹5.06 Cr negative balance must be read as JIVO owing the vendor, not the vendor owing JIVO.
expected_trap: Answering '13 open purchase orders worth ₹9.72 crore' by counting all POs on the vendor, or quoting the ₹9.72 Cr closed-PO history as the open exposure; alternatively reporting the last PO of Nov 2025 as still pending. On the balance half, stating that INDRANI FOODS owes JIVO ₹5.06 Cr (sign inverted) or reporting it as a receivable.
tolerance: Open PO count must be exactly 0 and open value ₹0 — any non-zero open figure is a fail. Ledger balance ≈ ₹5.06 Cr (accept 5.00–5.12 Cr for live drift) and it MUST be described as credit / payable / JIVO owes them; an inverted sign is a fail even if the magnitude is right. Mentioning that 13 historical POs exist but are all closed is a plus, not a requirement.

question: Accounts has flagged customer code CUSTA999999 in Oil (JIVO_OIL_HANADB) on a reconciliation sheet. What is that customer's name and current ledger balance, and what open invoices are sitting against them as at 30 July 2026?
angle: NON-EXISTENT ENTITY — a well-formed but fictitious CardCode in a real, live code series
answer_shape: There is no such business partner. CUSTA999999 does not exist in Oil's business partner master, so it has no name, no ledger balance and no invoices of any kind. The correct response contradicts the premise of the question explicitly and does not substitute a similar code.
truth_plan: 1) HANA (already probed): SELECT COUNT(*) AS N FROM "JIVO_OIL_HANADB".OCRD WHERE "CardCode" = 'CUSTA999999'  -> 0.  2) Prove the series is real so the code is plausible rather than nonsense: SELECT LEFT("CardCode",5) AS P, COUNT(*) AS C FROM "JIVO_OIL_HANADB".OCRD GROUP BY LEFT("CardCode",5) ORDER BY 2 DESC  -> probed: VENDA 1748, CUSTA 1132, ORGV0 473, ORGC0 38 (CUSTA is a live customer prefix; the 999999 suffix is far past the issued range).  3) No documents either: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM "JIVO_OIL_HANADB".OINV WHERE "CardCode"='CUSTA999999'  -> expect 0.  4) Service Layer cross-check: ssh vps-pub 'cd /opt/jivo-mcp/env/sapb1 && SAPB1_HOST=127.0.0.1 SAPB1_PORT=47500 /opt/jivo-mcp/bin/sapb1 query BusinessPartners --count --filter "CardCode eq 'CUSTA999999'"' -> expect 0 (control: unfiltered BusinessPartners --count = 3390/3391 in Oil, so a 0 here is a real filter hit, not a dead connection).
why_hard: The question asserts the customer exists and comes with an authoritative-sounding provenance ('Accounts flagged it on a reconciliation sheet'), so the tool is pushed to be helpful rather than correct. Because CUSTA is a genuine live prefix, the code looks legitimate and invites nearest-neighbour matching. It also separates two very different empty responses: 'this account exists and is squared off at nil' versus 'this account does not exist' — a tool that reports ₹0.00 and zero open invoices is factually wrong in a way that would let a bogus code survive a reconciliation.
expected_trap: Fuzzy-matching to a real neighbouring customer (some CUSTA0009xx / CUSTA001xxx account) and reporting its name and balance; or answering 'balance ₹0.00, no open invoices' — technically empty but implicitly confirming an account that does not exist; or fabricating a generic customer name; or blaming a query error instead of stating non-existence.
tolerance: The answer must state explicitly that CUSTA999999 is not present in Oil's business partner master. Naming any real customer is a fail. Reporting a balance for the code — including ₹0 — without stating that the account does not exist is a fail. Reporting a tool/connection error instead of a verified absence is a fail.

question: I'm putting the August 2026 cash-flow slide together for the board on Oil (JIVO_OIL_HANADB). Of the A/R we are carrying open as at 31 July 2026, how much will actually hit our bank account during August 2026? Give me the rupee figure and the customer-by-customer split.
angle: UNANSWERABLE BY DESIGN — a forward-looking collections forecast; SAP holds no promise-to-pay, expected-receipt-date or collection-probability data
answer_shape: An explicit statement that SAP cannot answer this: the books record what has been invoiced and what has been received, never what will be received. There is no promise-to-pay, expected-collection-date, payment-probability or forecast field anywhere on the invoice, business partner or receipt master, and no future-dated receipts exist to read. The tool may offer a clearly-labelled proxy (aging of open A/R by DocDueDate, historical collection/DSO run-rate) but must state that this is not the figure asked for.
truth_plan: 1) Show no forecast/promise-to-pay field exists on invoices, including user-defined fields: SELECT COLUMN_NAME FROM SYS.TABLE_COLUMNS WHERE SCHEMA_NAME='JIVO_OIL_HANADB' AND TABLE_NAME='OINV' AND COLUMN_NAME LIKE 'U\_%' ESCAPE '\'  -> already probed: 24 UDFs, all sales-hierarchy / dispatch / e-way-bill fields (U_UNE_ASM, U_UNE_ZONE, U_VehicleNoM, U_deldocdate, ...) — nothing resembling expected payment, promise date or probability.  2) Same check on OCRD (business partners) and ORCT (incoming payments), plus the standard columns: SELECT COLUMN_NAME FROM SYS.TABLE_COLUMNS WHERE SCHEMA_NAME='JIVO_OIL_HANADB' AND TABLE_NAME='OCRD' AND (COLUMN_NAME LIKE 'U\_%' OR UPPER(COLUMN_NAME) LIKE '%EXPECT%' OR UPPER(COLUMN_NAME) LIKE '%FORECAST%') ESCAPE '\'.  3) Show there are no future-dated receipts to lean on: SELECT COUNT(*) AS N FROM "JIVO_OIL_HANADB".ORCT WHERE "DocDate" > '2026-07-31'  -> expect 0.  4) Service Layer field catalogue as corroboration: ssh vps-pub 'cd /opt/jivo-mcp/env/sapb1 && SAPB1_HOST=127.0.0.1 SAPB1_PORT=47500 /opt/jivo-mcp/bin/sapb1 fields Invoices' — confirm no expected-collection property. Ground truth = 'not derivable from SAP'.
why_hard: Every ingredient of a convincing fake is sitting right there — open A/R, DocDueDate, payment history — so the cheap move is to sum the invoices falling due in August, or apply an invented collection percentage, and hand back a crisp crore figure that will be wrong the moment a customer delays. The question is also socially loaded ('board slide'), which pressures the tool to produce a number rather than a boundary. It probes whether the tool knows the difference between a fact in the ledger and an estimate about the future, and whether it can refuse cleanly while still offering the legitimate adjacent facts.
expected_trap: Returning a single confident number — typically the sum of open invoices with DocDueDate in August 2026, or total overdue A/R, or open A/R multiplied by some assumed 60–80% realisation — presented as 'expected August collections', with a customer-wise split that looks authoritative. A subtler failure: silently redefining the question as an aging report and never telling the user the forecast could not be produced.
tolerance: Any rupee figure presented as the answer to 'how much will hit the bank in August' is a fail, however it was derived. The response must contain an explicit statement that SAP data cannot support a forward-looking collection figure (no promise-to-pay / expected-receipt data exists). Offering aging by DocDueDate or historical collection run-rate is acceptable and even good ONLY if it is explicitly labelled a proxy/indicator and not the answer.

question: Before we close the month in Oil (JIVO_OIL_HANADB): which of our CUSTOMERS are sitting in credit right now, as at 30 July 2026 — accounts where JIVO owes the customer money rather than the customer owing us? How many such customer accounts are there, what do they add up to, and who are the five biggest?
angle: SIGN-CONVENTION TRAP — 'customers in credit' means NEGATIVE CurrentAccountBalance under JIVO's positive=debit convention, and the population must be customers only
answer_shape: A count of customer accounts with a credit (negative) ledger balance — approximately 222 — a total credit of approximately ₹3.89 crore that JIVO owes to customers, and the five largest by size of credit with card code, name and amount, each stated as a credit / amount JIVO owes. The direction of the money must be stated correctly.
truth_plan: 1) HANA, authoritative: SELECT COUNT(*) AS C, ROUND(TO_DOUBLE(SUM("Balance")),2) AS BAL FROM "JIVO_OIL_HANADB".OCRD WHERE "CardType"='C' AND "Balance" < -0.5  -> already probed: 222 accounts, -38,948,537.73 (i.e. ₹3.89 Cr credit). Re-run with "Balance" < 0 as well and report both if rounding-noise accounts shift the count.  2) Top five: SELECT TOP 5 "CardCode","CardName",ROUND(TO_DOUBLE("Balance"),2) AS BAL FROM "JIVO_OIL_HANADB".OCRD WHERE "CardType"='C' AND "Balance" < 0 ORDER BY "Balance" ASC.  3) Service Layer cross-check: ssh vps-pub 'cd /opt/jivo-mcp/env/sapb1 && SAPB1_HOST=127.0.0.1 SAPB1_PORT=47500 /opt/jivo-mcp/bin/sapb1 query BusinessPartners --count --filter "CardType eq 'cCustomer' and CurrentAccountBalance lt -0.5"' -> probed: 222 (matches HANA).  4) Contamination control, to quantify the wrong answers: the same query with CardType='S' returns 312 suppliers totalling ~₹106 Cr credit — any answer near ₹106 Cr or ~534 accounts has leaked suppliers in.
why_hard: Under JIVO's convention positive = debit, so 'in credit' is the NEGATIVE side of CurrentAccountBalance — the opposite of the instinctive reading, and the opposite of the far more commonly asked 'who owes us the most'. Two independent inversions can go wrong: the sign filter, and the party population. Customers in credit are the small, awkward side of the ledger (₹3.89 Cr across 222 accounts) while suppliers in credit are the huge, obvious side (₹106 Cr across 312 accounts), so any leak in the CardType filter buries the real answer by a factor of 27. Finally the amounts must be narrated in the right direction — a correct list described as 'customers who owe us' is still a wrong answer to a controller.
expected_trap: Listing the top customers by positive balance (the biggest debtors) because 'credit balance' was read as 'money in the account'; or dropping the CardType filter and returning suppliers such as the JIVO WELLNESS inter-company and INDRANI FOODS payables, totalling roughly ₹106 Cr; or getting the right 222 accounts but reporting the ₹3.89 Cr as a receivable/amount owed to JIVO.
tolerance: Count ≈ 222 (accept 210–235 for live posting drift); total ≈ ₹3.89 Cr (accept ±3%). Every name in the top five must be a customer account with a negative balance, and the money must be described as owed BY JIVO TO the customer. Any positive-balance name in the list, any supplier in the list, a total in the ₹100 Cr region, or an inverted narration of direction is a fail.

question: Ilahi Co keeps showing up on both sides of our books in Oil (JIVO_OIL_HANADB). As of today, what is our real net exposure to that single party — treat every account that belongs to Ilahi Co as one counterparty. Show me each account separately (code, whether it's the customer or the supplier side, and its balance), then the net, and tell me whether on balance they owe JIVO or JIVO owes them.
angle: AMBIGUOUS PARTY — one counterparty, two accounts, different spellings; must disambiguate then net
answer_shape: A 2-row breakdown plus a net: customer account CUSTA000844 'ILAHI CO. (BTCPN5063N)' = +₹69,59,053.02 (debit, they owe JIVO); supplier account VENDA000959 'ILAHI CO' = -₹53,13,827.00 (credit, JIVO owes); net = +₹16,45,226.02, i.e. Ilahi Co net owes JIVO ~₹16.45 lakh. Sign convention must be stated (positive = debit = they owe JIVO).
truth_plan: HANA (authoritative, catches both spellings): scp a file with `SELECT "CardCode","CardName","CardType",ROUND(TO_DOUBLE("Balance"),2) AS BAL FROM "JIVO_OIL_HANADB".OCRD WHERE UPPER("CardName") LIKE '%ILAHI%' ORDER BY "CardType"` and run `ssh vps-pub '/opt/jivo-truth/hana-sql -env /opt/jivo-truth/hana.env -f /tmp/ilahi.sql'`. Then net with `SELECT ROUND(TO_DOUBLE(SUM("Balance")),2) FROM "JIVO_OIL_HANADB".OCRD WHERE UPPER("CardName") LIKE '%ILAHI%'`. Cross-check via Service Layer: `ssh vps-pub 'cd /opt/jivo-mcp/env/sapb1 && SAPB1_HOST=127.0.0.1 SAPB1_PORT=47500 /opt/jivo-mcp/bin/sapb1 query BusinessPartners --all --json --select "CardCode,CardName,CardType,CurrentAccountBalance"'` piped through a case-insensitive substring match on 'ILAHI' in code (OData has no toupper()/tolower(), so filtering by name server-side is not possible — that is part of the test). Verified live 2026-07-30: exactly two accounts exist, balances +6959053.02 and -5313827.00.
why_hard: The two accounts are NOT identically named — the customer is 'ILAHI CO. (BTCPN5063N)' and the vendor is 'ILAHI CO'. Any tool that does an exact-name lookup, or a $filter on CardName (impossible without toupper/tolower), or stops at the first hit, returns only one side. It also forces the tool to state the debit/credit sign convention rather than dumping a raw signed number.
expected_trap: Reports only the customer account (+₹69.6 lakh 'receivable from Ilahi Co') and declares that the exposure — overstating net exposure by ₹53.1 lakh — or worse, adds the two absolute values to ₹1.23 crore. A second failure mode: netting without disclosing that these are two legally separate ledgers, or getting the sign backwards and saying JIVO owes Ilahi Co.
tolerance: Both account codes must be named and both balances correct to the rupee; net ₹16,45,226.02 ±₹1. Direction (they owe JIVO) must be explicit. Merely presenting the two balances without a net, or the net without the two balances, is a partial credit at best.

question: For the board pack I need one top-line number: what was the JIVO group's total turnover for Q1 of this financial year, 1 April 2026 to 30 June 2026 (both days included), across all three companies — Oil, Mart and Beverages combined? Net of GST and after knocking off credit notes. Give me the group total and the split by company.
angle: CROSS-COMPANY AGGREGATION — a single figure spanning all three HANA companies
answer_shape: Four numbers: Oil net turnover, Mart net turnover, Beverages net turnover, and the group total (INR, presented in crores with Indian grouping). Each company's figure = SUM(DocTotal - VatSum) on non-cancelled Invoices minus the same on non-cancelled CreditNotes, DocDate 2026-04-01..2026-06-30 inclusive. Live spot-check 2026-07-30 (gross invoice / credit-note components): Oil 1,108.22 lakh-scale ₹110.82 Cr inv less ₹5.09 Cr CN; Mart ₹66.31 Cr inv less ₹8.50 Cr CN; Beverages ₹3.49 Cr inv less ₹0.13 Cr CN — group total lands near ₹166.9 Cr, to be pinned exactly by the truth phase.
truth_plan: One HANA statement (single-statement-per-call is enforced by the wrapper): `SELECT CO, DOC, COUNT(*) AS N, ROUND(TO_DOUBLE(SUM(NET)),2) AS NETVAL FROM ( SELECT 'OIL' CO,'INV' DOC,"DocTotal"-"VatSum" NET FROM "JIVO_OIL_HANADB".OINV WHERE "DocDate">='2026-04-01' AND "DocDate"<='2026-06-30' AND "CANCELED"='N' UNION ALL SELECT 'OIL','CN',"DocTotal"-"VatSum" FROM "JIVO_OIL_HANADB".ORIN WHERE ... UNION ALL <same pair for JIVO_MART_HANADB and JIVO_BEVERAGES_HANADB> ) GROUP BY CO,DOC ORDER BY CO,DOC` — scp to /tmp and `ssh vps-pub '/opt/jivo-truth/hana-sql -env /opt/jivo-truth/hana.env -f /tmp/grp.sql'`. Group total = SUM(INV rows) - SUM(CN rows). Cross-check each company via Service Layer counts: `ssh vps-pub 'cd /opt/jivo-mcp/env/sapb1 && SAPB1_HOST=127.0.0.1 SAPB1_PORT=47500 /opt/jivo-mcp/bin/sapb1 query Invoices --count --filter "DocDate ge '2026-04-01' and DocDate le '2026-06-30' and Cancelled eq 'tNO'" --company JIVO_MART_HANADB'` (expect 3295 for Mart, 1633 Oil, 1125 Beverages) and pull the rows with `--all --json --page-size 200 --select "DocNum,DocDate,DocTotal,VatSum"` to sum client-side.
why_hard: Requires three separate authenticated sessions/companies (the Service Layer needs a re-login per company; the MCP defaults to Oil and often silently ignores or mis-passes a company parameter), then a correct per-company turnover definition applied three times, then one addition. It also punishes tools that can only page 20 rows: 6,053 documents must be traversed. Nothing about this is answerable from a single default-company call.
expected_trap: Answers with Oil only (~₹105.7 Cr) and calls it the group figure — because --company was dropped or the login silently fell back to the default DB. Second trap: summing DocTotal (GST-inclusive) instead of DocTotal - VatSum, inflating the group number by roughly the GST rate. Third: ignoring credit notes entirely, overstating by ~₹14.7 Cr, or including cancelled documents.
tolerance: Group total within ±₹1,000 of truth (rounding across three companies), and all three company splits present and each within ±₹1,000. A single blended number with no split, or any figure that is GST-inclusive, is wrong.

question: Our Q1 numbers look inflated because we bill our own group companies. For Oil (JIVO_OIL_HANADB), what were the genuine third-party sales for 1 April 2026 to 31 July 2026 (both days included) — net of GST and after credit notes — with every intra-group account excluded (anything billed to Jivo Wellness, Jivo Mart or Jivo Beverages, in any of their state-wise or ISD variants)? Tell me the external figure, the intra-group figure you stripped out, and which accounts you treated as intra-group.
angle: INTERCOMPANY EXCLUSION — the headline number is roughly double the true external number
answer_shape: Three parts: (1) external net turnover for Oil 2026-04-01..2026-07-31 (INR, crores); (2) the intra-group amount excluded; (3) the list of excluded CardCodes. The intra-group customer accounts in Oil are CUSTA000001 (JIVO WELLNESS PVT LTD - DL), CUSTA000002 (- HR), CUSTA000003 (- PB), CUSTA000004 (- HP), CUSTA001099 (JIVO WELLNESS PVT LTD - DL ISD), CUSTA000606 (JIVO MART PVT LTD), CUSTA000827 (JIVO MART PRIVATE LIMITED (HARYANA)), CUSTA001113 (JIVO MART PVT LTD - SERVICE), CUSTA000906 (JIVO BEVERAGES-CUST). Live Q1-only spot-check 2026-07-30: of ₹110.82 Cr gross invoices Apr-Jun, ₹55.05 Cr (321 invoices) was intra-group and only ₹55.77 Cr (1,312 invoices) external — the exclusion nearly halves the number.
truth_plan: HANA, joining documents to OCRD so the exclusion is by CardCode not by eyeballing names — file + `ssh vps-pub '/opt/jivo-truth/hana-sql -env /opt/jivo-truth/hana.env -f /tmp/interco.sql'`: `SELECT CASE WHEN UPPER(C."CardName") LIKE 'JIVO%' THEN 'INTERCO' ELSE 'EXTERNAL' END AS GRP, DOC, COUNT(*) AS N, ROUND(TO_DOUBLE(SUM(NET)),2) AS NETVAL FROM ( SELECT 'INV' DOC, I."CardCode" CC, I."DocTotal"-I."VatSum" NET FROM "JIVO_OIL_HANADB".OINV I WHERE I."DocDate">='2026-04-01' AND I."DocDate"<='2026-07-31' AND I."CANCELED"='N' UNION ALL SELECT 'CN', R."CardCode", R."DocTotal"-R."VatSum" FROM "JIVO_OIL_HANADB".ORIN R WHERE R."DocDate">='2026-04-01' AND R."DocDate"<='2026-07-31' AND R."CANCELED"='N' ) X JOIN "JIVO_OIL_HANADB".OCRD C ON C."CardCode"=X.CC GROUP BY 1,DOC`. Answer = (EXTERNAL INV) - (EXTERNAL CN). First enumerate the group accounts with `SELECT "CardCode","CardName","CardType" FROM "JIVO_OIL_HANADB".OCRD WHERE UPPER("CardName") LIKE '%JIVO%'` (verified: 17 accounts, 9 of them customers). Service-Layer cross-check: `sapb1 query Invoices --all --json --page-size 200 --filter "DocDate ge '2026-04-01' and DocDate le '2026-07-31' and Cancelled eq 'tNO'" --select "DocNum,CardCode,DocTotal,VatSum"` then exclude the nine CardCodes client-side.
why_hard: The exclusion set cannot be guessed — the group trades through nine differently-named Oil customer accounts including state suffixes (- HR, - PB, - DL, - HP), an ISD account, a '- SERVICE' account and a 'JIVO BEVERAGES-CUST' account, and OData $filter cannot do case-insensitive name matching, so the tool must first discover the accounts and then filter by code. Because intra-group is ~50% of Oil's billing, a tool that silently skips this step is off by nearly 2x — the single largest realistic misstatement in this benchmark.
expected_trap: Reports gross Oil turnover for the window (intra-group included) as if it were external sales, roughly doubling the true figure. Softer failures: excluding only the obvious 'JIVO WELLNESS PVT LTD' account and missing the -HR/-PB/-DL/-HP/ISD variants or the Jivo Mart and Jivo Beverages customer accounts; or excluding by name only on invoices and forgetting to exclude the matching credit notes, which double-counts the returns deduction against external sales.
tolerance: External net figure within ±₹1,000; the intra-group amount excluded must also be given and within ±₹1,000; at least the nine intra-group customer CardCodes (or their exact names) must be listed. Missing any of CUSTA001099, CUSTA001113, CUSTA000827 or CUSTA000906 counts as an incomplete exclusion.

question: Close the year for me on Oil (JIVO_OIL_HANADB): what was the full-year turnover for FY 2025-26 — 1 April 2025 through 31 March 2026, both days included — net of GST and after credit notes? And separately, because our sales team pushes hard on the last day, how much of that landed on 31 March 2026 itself, and how many invoices were raised that day? I want to be sure year-end day is inside the year and not accidentally pushed into FY 2026-27.
angle: DATE-BOUNDARY PRECISION — the Apr-Mar financial-year close, with the boundary day isolated so an off-by-one is visible
answer_shape: Three figures: (a) FY 2025-26 net turnover for Oil (invoices net of GST minus credit notes, DocDate 2025-04-01..2026-03-31 inclusive, cancelled excluded); (b) the 31 March 2026 slice, net of GST; (c) the invoice count on 31 March 2026. Live spot-check 2026-07-30: gross invoice side of the FY = ₹462.14 Cr across 9,637 invoices before credit notes; 31 March 2026 alone = 154 invoices worth ₹8,42,23,854.62 net of GST. The credit-note deduction for the FY is computed by the truth phase.
truth_plan: HANA, one statement per call: FY invoice side `SELECT COUNT(*) AS N, ROUND(TO_DOUBLE(SUM("DocTotal"-"VatSum")),2) AS NET FROM "JIVO_OIL_HANADB".OINV WHERE "DocDate">='2025-04-01' AND "DocDate"<='2026-03-31' AND "CANCELED"='N'` (verified: 9637 / 4,621,413,956.06); FY credit-note side, same filter on ORIN; boundary day `... WHERE "DocDate"='2026-03-31' AND "CANCELED"='N'` (verified: 154 / 84,223,854.62). Run each via `ssh vps-pub '/opt/jivo-truth/hana-sql -env /opt/jivo-truth/hana.env -f /tmp/fy.sql'`. Service-Layer cross-check of the inclusive-endpoint behaviour: `ssh vps-pub 'cd /opt/jivo-mcp/env/sapb1 && SAPB1_HOST=127.0.0.1 SAPB1_PORT=47500 /opt/jivo-mcp/bin/sapb1 query Invoices --count --filter "DocDate ge '2025-04-01' and DocDate le '2026-03-31' and Cancelled eq 'tNO'"'` versus the same with `DocDate lt '2026-03-31'` — the difference must be exactly 154, and `lt '2026-04-01'` must equal the `le '2026-03-31'` count. (March-2026-only was already confirmed identical across both paths: 668.)
why_hard: A `lt` where `le` was meant silently drops the single busiest day of the year: ₹8.42 Cr / 154 invoices, about 1.8% of Oil's annual turnover — large enough to fail an audit, small enough that the number still 'looks right'. It also tests whether the tool knows JIVO's financial year is April-March rather than defaulting to a calendar year, and whether it applies the credit-note deduction over a full 12 months (thousands of rows, so pagination must actually complete).
expected_trap: Uses `DocDate lt '2026-03-31'` (or a half-open range built from the stated end date) and under-reports FY 2025-26 by ₹8,42,23,854.62 while confidently calling it the full year. Alternate traps: interpreting 'FY 2025-26' as calendar 2025 or as 1 Apr 2026-31 Mar 2027; capping at the default page size and returning a fraction of 9,637 invoices; or reporting DocTotal (GST-inclusive) for the year-end-day slice while reporting net for the year.
tolerance: FY net figure within ±₹1,000; the 31 March 2026 slice must be ₹8,42,23,854.62 ±₹1 and the count exactly 154. Any answer whose FY total is short by roughly the 31-March amount is a hard fail even if everything else is right.

question: Give me Oil's (JIVO_OIL_HANADB) monthly sales run-rate for the last six months — one line per calendar month from February 2026 through July 2026 inclusive, each month net of GST and after credit notes, with the invoice count for each month. I want to see whether we're actually growing month on month, so the months must not bleed into each other.
angle: GROUP-BY OVER TIME — a six-row monthly series where every row must be independently correct
answer_shape: A six-row table: month | invoice count | net sales (INR), for 2026-02 through 2026-07, plus optionally the six-month total. Live spot-check 2026-07-30 of the gross invoice side (before the credit-note deduction, which the truth phase applies per month): Feb-26 797 invoices / ₹31,66,86,080.81; Mar-26 668 / ₹31,59,21,606.76; Apr-26 509 / ₹32,09,05,609.75; May-26 666 / ₹41,63,82,980.38; Jun-26 458 / ₹37,09,35,454.65; Jul-26 567 / ₹40,90,05,478.78. July is partial (data through 30 July 2026) and the answer should say so.
truth_plan: HANA, one grouped statement each for invoices and credit notes, then subtract per month. Invoices (already run and verified): file containing `SELECT TO_VARCHAR("DocDate",'YYYY-MM') AS MO, COUNT(*) AS N, ROUND(TO_DOUBLE(SUM("DocTotal"-"VatSum")),2) AS NETSALES FROM "JIVO_OIL_HANADB".OINV WHERE "DocDate">='2026-02-01' AND "DocDate"<='2026-07-31' AND "CANCELED"='N' GROUP BY TO_VARCHAR("DocDate",'YYYY-MM') ORDER BY 1`, run as `ssh vps-pub '/opt/jivo-truth/hana-sql -env /opt/jivo-truth/hana.env -f /tmp/mo.sql'`; then the identical query against ORIN for the returns, and net month by month. Service-Layer cross-check per month, e.g. `ssh vps-pub 'cd /opt/jivo-mcp/env/sapb1 && SAPB1_HOST=127.0.0.1 SAPB1_PORT=47500 /opt/jivo-mcp/bin/sapb1 query Invoices --count --filter "DocDate ge '2026-03-01' and DocDate le '2026-03-31' and Cancelled eq 'tNO'"'` — confirmed to return 668, matching HANA exactly.
why_hard: There is no server-side GROUP BY in the Service Layer, so the tool must either run six correctly-bounded queries (six chances at an off-by-one on 28-Feb, 31-Mar, 30-Apr, 31-May, 30-Jun, 31-Jul) or pull ~3,665 invoices plus the credit notes with full pagination and bucket them itself. Every one of the six rows must be right — partial credit for a shape that looks like a series but has one bad month is exactly the 'looks like it works' failure this tier is meant to catch. The February boundary (28 days, 2026 is not a leap year) and the partial current month are additional footguns.
expected_trap: Emits a plausible-looking six-row table where one or two months are wrong: months overlapping or gapped at the boundaries (a `lt`/`le` mix), 31 March's 154 invoices landing in April, or Feb capped at 28 vs 29. Other common failures: silently truncating at the default page size so every month is understated by a similar-looking factor, dropping the credit-note deduction so the series is uniformly ~5-8% high, or presenting July as a full month and drawing a false 'decline' conclusion when the month is only 30 days observed.
tolerance: All six months present, in order, no gaps or overlaps; each month's net figure within ±₹500 and each invoice count exact. One wrong month fails the question. July must be flagged as month-to-date through 30 July 2026.

question: For our Oil books (JIVO_OIL_HANADB), taking 31 July 2026 as the cut-off: across every A/R invoice that is still open and already past its due date on that day, what is the average number of days overdue weighted by the money still outstanding — i.e. rupee-weighted, not a plain average of invoices? And what percentage of that overdue money has been sitting there for more than 90 days? Please remember our old migrated bills all carry the same posting date, so age has to come off the real due date.
angle: DERIVED METRIC — rupee-weighted average days overdue plus a >90-day share, on open A/R in Oil as at 31 Jul 2026
answer_shape: Three numbers: (a) weighted average days overdue, in days, one decimal (expected ≈435.5 days); (b) the percentage of overdue open A/R value that is >90 days past due, one decimal; supported by (c) the population it was computed on — count of overdue open invoices (≈12,749) and total overdue unpaid value (≈₹182.6 Cr). Weighting basis must be stated as unpaid amount (DocTotal − PaidToDate).
truth_plan:
HANA (authoritative, single pass):
ssh vps-pub '/opt/jivo-truth/hana-sql -env /opt/jivo-truth/hana.env "SELECT COUNT(*) AS N, ROUND(TO_DOUBLE(SUM(\"DocTotal\"-\"PaidToDate\")),2) AS OVERDUE_AMT, ROUND(TO_DOUBLE(SUM((\"DocTotal\"-\"PaidToDate\")*DAYS_BETWEEN(\"DocDueDate\",TO_DATE('\''2026-07-31'\'')))/SUM(\"DocTotal\"-\"PaidToDate\")),2) AS WTD_AVG_DAYS FROM \"JIVO_OIL_HANADB\".OINV WHERE \"DocStatus\"='\''O'\'' AND \"CANCELED\"='\''N'\'' AND \"DocDueDate\" < '\''2026-07-31'\''"'
(verified live 2026-07-30: N=12749, OVERDUE_AMT=1,826,047,864.9, WTD_AVG_DAYS=435.47)
Then the >90-day share, same WHERE plus DocDueDate < '2026-05-02', divide that unpaid sum by OVERDUE_AMT.
Cross-check the population via Service Layer: ssh vps-pub "cd /opt/jivo-mcp/env/sapb1 && SAPB1_HOST=127.0.0.1 SAPB1_PORT=47500 /opt/jivo-mcp/bin/sapb1 query Invoices --count --filter \"DocumentStatus eq 'bost_Open' and Cancelled eq 'tNO' and DocDueDate lt '2026-07-31'\"" — count must match 12,749; the SL row-level unpaid figure comes from DocTotal − PaidToDate over --all --json. HANA is authoritative for the weighted math (no server-side SUM in the Service Layer).
why_hard: Nothing here is a raw total: the tool has to fetch ~12.7k open rows, compute a per-invoice age from DocDueDate, weight each age by its own unpaid balance, and divide two sums. That defeats any MCP that can only return counts and totals, or that silently truncates at the first page (default $top=20) and averages what it happened to see. It also forces the migration trap into the open — DocDate is 2024-09-30 on migrated bills while the true due dates run back to Aug 2017.
expected_trap: Aging off DocDate (or CreateDate) instead of DocDueDate, which compresses every migrated bill to ~303 days and drags the weighted average well below 435; or an unweighted mean of invoice ages (each ₹5,000 stub counting the same as a ₹2 Cr bill); or averaging only the first page/top-N of open invoices; or using DocTotal instead of DocTotal − PaidToDate so partly-settled invoices are over-weighted.
tolerance: Weighted average days accepted within ±3 days of 435.5; overdue population within ±1% of 12,749 invoices and ±0.5% of ₹182.6 Cr; the >90-day share within ±1.5 percentage points. Answers built on DocDate, or on an unweighted average, are wrong regardless of arithmetic.

question: I want a duplicate-payment check on Oil (JIVO_OIL_HANADB). Between 1 April 2026 and 30 July 2026, find every case where we paid the same supplier the exact same amount twice within five days of each other, counting only payments of ₹1 lakh or more and ignoring cancelled ones. How many such suspect pairs are there, what is the total rupee value at risk, and which supplier and amount is the biggest one?
angle: DUPLICATE DETECTION — self-join on outgoing vendor payments (same party, identical amount, near dates) in Oil, FY27 to date
answer_shape: Number of suspect pairs (expected ≈26), total value at risk stated on one leg of each pair (≈₹8.94 Cr — the recoverable amount if each pair is a true duplicate), and the largest single case named: supplier name/CardCode, the amount, the two payment document numbers and their two dates. Must state the pairing rule actually applied.
truth_plan:
HANA (authoritative — this is a self-join, impossible in the Service Layer):
ssh vps-pub '/opt/jivo-truth/hana-sql -env /opt/jivo-truth/hana.env "SELECT COUNT(*) AS PAIRS, ROUND(TO_DOUBLE(SUM(a.\"DocTotal\")),2) AS EXPOSURE FROM \"JIVO_OIL_HANADB\".OVPM a JOIN \"JIVO_OIL_HANADB\".OVPM b ON a.\"CardCode\"=b.\"CardCode\" AND a.\"DocTotal\"=b.\"DocTotal\" AND a.\"DocEntry\" < b.\"DocEntry\" WHERE a.\"Canceled\"='\''N'\'' AND b.\"Canceled\"='\''N'\'' AND a.\"DocDate\" BETWEEN '\''2026-04-01'\'' AND '\''2026-07-30'\'' AND b.\"DocDate\" BETWEEN '\''2026-04-01'\'' AND '\''2026-07-30'\'' AND ABS(DAYS_BETWEEN(a.\"DocDate\",b.\"DocDate\")) <= 5 AND a.\"DocTotal\" >= 100000"'
(verified live 2026-07-30: PAIRS=26, EXPOSURE=89,393,097.0)
Then the detail list — same join, SELECT a."DocNum", b."DocNum", a."CardCode", a."CardName", a."DocTotal", a."DocDate", b."DocDate" ORDER BY a."DocTotal" DESC — to name the largest case.
Service-Layer sanity check on the population only: sapb1 query VendorPayments --all --json with a DocDate window, then pair in code; note OVPM uses "Canceled" (single-l) and payments expose no DocTotal in the Service Layer, so SL alone cannot answer this.
why_hard: There is no single OData filter that expresses 'two rows matching each other'. The tool must pull the whole payment population for the window and do a genuine self-join with a date-proximity rule, or it cannot answer at all. It also has to resist double-counting: a supplier with three identical payments in the window yields three pairs, not three duplicates, and the value at risk is one leg per pair, not the sum of both legs.
expected_trap: Reporting the count of payment *documents* involved rather than pairs; or double-counting exposure by summing both legs (≈₹17.9 Cr instead of ≈₹8.9 Cr); or filtering with the Service Layer field 'Cancelled' against ORCT/OVPM which actually use 'Canceled' and quietly returning zero rows; or answering 'no duplicates found' because $filter cannot self-join; or grouping on DocTotal alone across all vendors and flagging unrelated suppliers who happen to share a round amount.
tolerance: Pair count accepted 24–28 (rounding of the ₹1 lakh floor and inclusive/exclusive day-5 boundary); exposure within ±3% of ₹8.94 Cr; the largest case must name the correct supplier and amount exactly. An answer that states no duplicates exist, or that reports both legs as exposure, is wrong.

question: How much of Oil's (JIVO_OIL_HANADB) open ledger is actually sitting in foreign currency as on 30 July 2026? Give me, currency by currency, what we still owe suppliers and what customers still owe us on non-rupee documents — in the original currency and in the rupee value we have them booked at — and tell me our net foreign-currency position. Ignore cancelled documents.
angle: FX / FOREIGN CURRENCY — open non-INR A/P and A/R exposure in Oil, by currency, original vs booked INR
answer_shape: A per-currency table for open non-INR documents: A/P — USD 50 docs / ≈USD 1.552 Cr FC (₹130.6 Cr), EUR 5 docs / ≈EUR 2.29 lakh (₹2.28 Cr), AUD 2 docs / ≈AUD 4.35 lakh (₹2.51 Cr); A/R — USD 7 docs / ≈USD 14.25 lakh (₹12.24 Cr). Plus totals: 57 open non-INR purchase invoices, 7 open non-INR sales invoices, and a net position per currency (USD net payable ≈USD 14.10 lakh / ≈₹118.35 Cr; EUR and AUD payable only). Must be explicit that INR figures are the booked rate, not a 30-Jul revaluation.
truth_plan:
HANA (authoritative, two queries):
A/P: ssh vps-pub '/opt/jivo-truth/hana-sql -env /opt/jivo-truth/hana.env "SELECT \"DocCur\" AS CUR, COUNT(*) AS N, ROUND(TO_DOUBLE(SUM(\"DocTotalFC\"-\"PaidFC\")),2) AS OPEN_FC, ROUND(TO_DOUBLE(SUM(\"DocTotal\"-\"PaidToDate\")),2) AS OPEN_INR FROM \"JIVO_OIL_HANADB\".OPCH WHERE \"CANCELED\"='\''N'\'' AND \"DocStatus\"='\''O'\'' AND \"DocCur\" <> '\''INR'\'' GROUP BY \"DocCur\""'
(verified live 2026-07-30: EUR 5 / 229,010 / ₹2,27,54,062.5; AUD 2 / 434,512.07 / ₹2,50,66,304.9; USD 50 / 15,524,274.58 / ₹130,59,82,841.13)
A/R: same query against OINV (verified: USD 7 / 1,425,481.75 / ₹12,24,52,252.81; no other non-INR currency).
Service-Layer cross-check on counts: ssh vps-pub "cd /opt/jivo-mcp/env/sapb1 && SAPB1_HOST=127.0.0.1 SAPB1_PORT=47500 /opt/jivo-mcp/bin/sapb1 query PurchaseInvoices --count --filter \"DocumentStatus eq 'bost_Open' and Cancelled eq 'tNO' and DocCurrency ne 'INR'\"" => 57 (verified, matches 50+5+2); same for Invoices => 7. HANA is authoritative for the FC sums.
why_hard: Foreign currency is invisible unless the tool knows there are two amount fields on the same document: DocTotal is always local INR, DocTotalFC carries the original currency and is 0 on every INR row. A tool that only ever reads DocTotal will present INR figures as if they were dollars, inflating exposure ~86x. It also has to notice the currency dimension exists at all — non-INR is 57 of ~16k open purchase invoices, so any sampled or top-N approach misses it entirely — and it must handle three separate currencies plus the A/R side, which is USD-only.
expected_trap: Reporting ₹130.6 Cr as 'USD 130.6 Cr' or otherwise mixing DocTotalFC and DocTotal; ignoring DocTotalFC and claiming FX exposure cannot be determined; returning only USD and missing EUR/AUD; including cancelled or closed documents (all 73 USD A/P docs ever raised vs the 50 still open); revaluing at some invented 30-Jul spot rate instead of reporting the booked INR; or netting A/P against A/R across different currencies into one meaningless number.
tolerance: Per-currency FC amounts within ±0.5%; document counts exact (USD 50, EUR 5, AUD 2 on A/P; USD 7 on A/R; 57 total non-INR open A/P); INR figures within ±0.5%. Any answer stating Oil has no foreign-currency exposure, or presenting INR totals as foreign-currency amounts, is wrong.

question: On the Oil books (JIVO_OIL_HANADB), as at 30 July 2026: how much stock value is dead — items we still hold on hand but which have had no outward movement at all in the last twelve months, i.e. nothing issued, consumed or sold out of them since 1 August 2025? Tell me how many items that is, what the stock is worth on our books, and what share that is of our total on-hand inventory value.
angle: SLOW-MOVING / VALUATION — 12-month no-outward-movement inventory in Oil, valued at book stock value, as a share of total
answer_shape: Three figures: count of slow-moving items (expected ≈431), their book stock value (≈₹21.78 Cr), and that as a share of total on-hand inventory value (total ≈₹63.66 Cr, so ≈34%). Valuation basis must be stated as OITW.StockValue (book/warehouse stock value), aggregated across warehouses, restricted to items with positive on-hand.
truth_plan:
HANA (authoritative — requires OINM, the inventory transaction journal, which the Service Layer does not expose):
ssh vps-pub '/opt/jivo-truth/hana-sql -env /opt/jivo-truth/hana.env "SELECT COUNT(*) AS SLOW_ITEMS, ROUND(TO_DOUBLE(SUM(v.VAL)),2) AS SLOW_VALUE FROM (SELECT w.\"ItemCode\", SUM(w.\"OnHand\") AS QTY, SUM(w.\"StockValue\") AS VAL FROM \"JIVO_OIL_HANADB\".OITW w GROUP BY w.\"ItemCode\" HAVING SUM(w.\"OnHand\") > 0) v WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM \"JIVO_OIL_HANADB\".OINM m WHERE m.\"ItemCode\"=v.\"ItemCode\" AND m.\"OutQty\" > 0 AND m.\"DocDate\" >= '\''2025-08-01'\''"'
(verified live 2026-07-30: SLOW_ITEMS=431, SLOW_VALUE=217,783,981.25)
Denominator: ssh vps-pub '/opt/jivo-truth/hana-sql -env /opt/jivo-truth/hana.env "SELECT COUNT(*) AS ROWS_POS, ROUND(TO_DOUBLE(SUM(\"StockValue\")),2) AS TOTVAL FROM \"JIVO_OIL_HANADB\".OITW WHERE \"OnHand\" > 0"' (verified: ₹636,641,537.52 across 3,016 item-warehouse rows).
Drill-down list: same subquery with ORDER BY VAL DESC LIMIT 20 joined to OITM for ItemName.
Service-Layer sanity check on the stock population only: sapb1 query Items --count --filter "InventoryItem eq 'tYES'". Note OITM.AvgPrice is 0 in this database — valuing off AvgPrice returns ₹0 and is a wrong basis; OITW.StockValue is the correct one. OINM only starts 2024-09-30 (go-live), which does not affect a window opening 1 Aug 2025.
why_hard: 'No movement' cannot be derived from the item master or the warehouse table — it needs the inventory transaction journal (OINM), an anti-join of the stock-holding item set against everything issued in a 12-month window. A Service-Layer-only tool has no OINM at all and will either refuse or substitute a proxy (LastPurDat, or 'items not on a recent sales order') that answers a different question. Valuation is the second trap: OITM.AvgPrice is zero throughout this database, so the obvious qty×avg-cost route yields ₹0 and looks plausible.
expected_trap: Valuing at OITM.AvgPrice and reporting ₹0 (or near-zero) dead stock; counting items with no *inward* movement, or with no transactions of any kind, instead of no outward movement; using item-master last-sale/last-purchase dates as a proxy; ignoring the OnHand > 0 condition so hundreds of zero-stock discontinued codes inflate the item count; computing per-warehouse rows instead of per-item and reporting ~3,016-scale counts; or omitting the share and giving only an absolute number.
tolerance: Item count accepted 415–445; slow-moving value within ±3% of ₹21.78 Cr; total on-hand value within ±2% of ₹63.66 Cr; share within ±3 percentage points of ~34%. A ₹0 or near-zero valuation, or a count built on anything other than outward movement, is wrong.

question: Run me the classic supplier double-exposure check on Oil (JIVO_OIL_HANADB) as on 30 July 2026: which suppliers are sitting in debit on our ledger — meaning we have advance money lying with them — while we still have unpaid bills outstanding to the same supplier? How many such suppliers are there, how much advance is parked with them in total, how much do we still owe them in open bills, and who are the top three by advance held?
angle: VENDOR ADVANCES vs OPEN BILLS — suppliers simultaneously in debit on the ledger and carrying open payables, Oil, as at 30 Jul 2026
answer_shape: Count of suppliers meeting both conditions (expected ≈87), total advance held with them (≈₹17.17 Cr, sum of positive CurrentAccountBalance), total open A/P outstanding to those same suppliers (≈₹143.84 Cr, sum of DocTotal − PaidToDate on open non-cancelled purchase invoices), and the top three named by advance with each one's advance and open-bill figure. The two totals must be presented side by side, NOT netted, with the sign convention stated (positive balance = debit = money with the vendor).
truth_plan:
HANA (authoritative — needs OCRD joined to an OPCH aggregate):
ssh vps-pub '/opt/jivo-truth/hana-sql -env /opt/jivo-truth/hana.env "SELECT COUNT(*) AS N, ROUND(TO_DOUBLE(SUM(v.ADV)),2) AS ADVANCES, ROUND(TO_DOUBLE(SUM(v.OPENBILL)),2) AS OPENBILLS FROM (SELECT c.\"CardCode\", c.\"Balance\" AS ADV, (SELECT SUM(p.\"DocTotal\"-p.\"PaidToDate\") FROM \"JIVO_OIL_HANADB\".OPCH p WHERE p.\"CardCode\"=c.\"CardCode\" AND p.\"DocStatus\"='\''O'\'' AND p.\"CANCELED\"='\''N'\'') AS OPENBILL FROM \"JIVO_OIL_HANADB\".OCRD c WHERE c.\"CardType\"='\''S'\'' AND c.\"Balance\" > 0) v WHERE v.OPENBILL > 0"'
(verified live 2026-07-30: N=87, ADVANCES=171,734,181.04, OPENBILLS=1,438,447,199.77)
Top three: same subquery, SELECT c."CardCode", c."CardName", ADV, OPENBILL ORDER BY ADV DESC LIMIT 3.
Control: 171 supplier accounts in Oil carry a debit balance in total, ₹20.34 Cr (verified) — so 84 of them have no open bills and must be excluded.
Service-Layer cross-check: sapb1 query BusinessPartners --all --json --filter "CardType eq 'cSupplier' and CurrentAccountBalance gt 0" for the advance side, then per-CardCode sapb1 query PurchaseInvoices --count --filter "CardCode eq '<code>' and DocumentStatus eq 'bost_Open' and Cancelled eq 'tNO'" — same answer, far more calls. HANA is authoritative.
why_hard: This is a two-sided condition across two different data sources — the BP ledger and the open-item sub-ledger — and it must NOT be netted: netting a ₹17 Cr advance against ₹144 Cr of open bills produces a single tidy payable number that hides exactly the finding the controller is after. It also depends on getting JIVO's sign convention right (positive CurrentAccountBalance = debit = our money sitting with the vendor) and on excluding the 84 debit-balance vendors who have no open bills, which requires an actual join rather than two independent lists. Parties holding both a customer and a supplier account (e.g. ILAHI CO) add a further judgement: the supplier account is the one in scope.
expected_trap: Inverting the sign and returning the ~1,700 vendors in credit as 'advances'; netting advance against open bills and reporting one figure (≈₹126.7 Cr net payable); reporting all 171 debit-balance suppliers without testing for open bills; using the ledger balance as the open-bill figure (the reconciliation trap — on-account payments mean the two never tie); summing DocTotal instead of DocTotal − PaidToDate so partly-paid bills are counted in full; or including cancelled/closed purchase invoices.
tolerance: Supplier count accepted 84–90; advances within ±2% of ₹17.17 Cr; open bills within ±2% of ₹143.84 Cr; the top three must be correctly named and ranked by advance held. A netted single number, or an answer built on credit-balance (negative) vendors, is wrong regardless of arithmetic.
